fallback: I don't have that in my notes, so I won't guess. I can answer questions about Vamsikrishna's experience, skills, certifications, availability and the portfolio demos. For anything else, please contact him directly on LinkedIn.

topics.title: Who is Vamsikrishna?
topics.answer: Vamsikrishna Gollapudi is an Azure DevOps Engineer and Site Reliability Engineer with 9+ years in IT, based in Bengaluru, India. He started in Linux and Windows Server administration, then moved into Azure infrastructure, CI/CD automation, Kubernetes (AKS) and SRE. He currently works as a Site Reliability Engineer at Nexamatic Software Solutions.
more: His work has covered life sciences, banking and asset-management clients. Recent highlights: an 8-subscription Azure landing zone with 600+ resources at 99.95% availability, ~120 repositories migrated to GitHub Enterprise, and MTTR reduced by about 35%.
He is looking for 100% remote roles only, with a 15-day notice period.

topics.title: Availability and remote-only preference
topics.answer: He is open to 100% remote roles only: fully remote or permanent work-from-home, remote from India, or international remote roles that hire from India. He is not considering hybrid, onsite or office-based roles. Notice period: 15 days. He is based in Bengaluru, India.
more: Target roles, in order: Azure DevOps Engineer / Site Reliability Engineer, Azure Cloud or Infrastructure Engineer, Platform Engineer. He has worked with distributed teams across time zones.

topics.title: How to contact him
topics.answer: The best way to reach Vamsikrishna is LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/vamsikrishna-gollapudi. His GitHub is github.com/gollapudivamsi18. The contact section of this page has his email. A Naukri profile is available on request; there is no public Naukri link.

topics.title: Work experience
topics.answer:
9+ years in IT (Oct 2015 to present) across five roles, most recent first:
- Site Reliability Engineer, Nexamatic Software Solutions (Jan 2025 – present)
- Azure DevOps Engineer, Kumaran Systems (Apr 2024 – Jan 2025)
- Cloud Infrastructure Engineer, UST Global (May 2022 – Jun 2023)
- Tech Lead, Cognizant (Dec 2020 – Apr 2021)
- System Administrator (Linux & Windows), Anewa Engineering (Oct 2015 – Dec 2020)
more: Ask about any role by name, for example "What does he do at Nexamatic?" or "What did he do at UST Global?"

topics.title: Current role: SRE at Nexamatic
topics.answer: Since Jan 2025 he has been a Site Reliability Engineer at Nexamatic Software Solutions, supporting life-sciences clients. He designed and operates an 8-subscription Azure landing zone (600+ resources) at 99.95% availability and runs 6 production AKS clusters (180+ nodes, 300+ pods).
more: He led the migration of ~120 repositories and 45 teams from Azure Repos to GitHub Enterprise with under 30 minutes of developer downtime, and converted 60+ classic release pipelines into GitHub Actions and multi-stage Azure DevOps YAML, cutting new-service onboarding from ~3 days to under 4 hours.

On reliability: SLIs, SLOs, error budgets and 40+ runbooks reduced MTTR by ~35%; Prometheus, Grafana, Azure Monitor and Log Analytics with 150+ alert rules cut alert noise by 40%. On security: Defender for Cloud Secure Score went from 62% to 85%, and 200+ vulnerable builds were blocked before production.

topics.title: Azure DevOps Engineer at Kumaran Systems
topics.answer: From Apr 2024 to Jan 2025 he was an Azure DevOps Engineer at Kumaran Systems for a banking client. He built Azure DevOps build and release pipelines for 35+ services with approval gates and change-management checks, giving full audit traceability.
more: He introduced Terraform for networks, storage and VMs across 4 environments (setup went from ~3 days to 4 hours), migrated 40 classic releases to YAML (maintenance effort halved), containerised 15 services for AKS with Helm, and moved deployments from bi-weekly to 3 a week while keeping change-failure rate under 5%.

topics.title: Cloud Infrastructure Engineer at UST Global
topics.answer: From May 2022 to Jun 2023 he was a Cloud Infrastructure Engineer at UST Global for an asset-management client. He built and supported an Azure IaaS/PaaS estate of 250+ resources and rehosted 45 on-premises Windows and Linux servers to Azure across 5 waves with zero data loss.
more: He engineered hub-and-spoke networking with VPN links to 2 data centres, set up Azure Backup and Site Recovery for 60 critical workloads (4-hour RTO, 15-minute RPO in DR drills), raised Defender for Cloud compliance from 70% to 96%, and lowered monthly Azure spend by ~18% through right-sizing.

topics.title: Tech Lead at Cognizant
topics.answer: From Dec 2020 to Apr 2021 he was a Tech Lead at Cognizant on an on-premises-to-Azure migration for a life-sciences client. He assessed 180+ servers with Azure Migrate, planned 6 migration waves with cutover and rollback runbooks, and led a 5-member team through the lift-and-shift of 120 servers with 98% first-attempt cutover success.

topics.title: System Administrator at Anewa Engineering
topics.answer: From Oct 2015 to Dec 2020 he was a System Administrator (Linux & Windows) at Anewa Engineering. He administered 150+ RHEL, Ubuntu and Windows Server systems for 1,200 users at 99.9% uptime, managed Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS and DHCP, and kept patch compliance at 97%.

topics.title: Skills, in priority order
topics.answer:
In priority order:
1. Azure DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering: Azure Pipelines, GitHub Actions, GitHub Enterprise, Terraform, Bicep, AKS, Helm, Prometheus, Grafana, Azure Monitor, KQL, SLOs.
2. Azure Cloud Infrastructure: networking, Entra ID, RBAC, Azure Policy, Key Vault, Defender for Cloud, Azure Migrate, Site Recovery, Backup.
3. Windows Server administration: Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, PowerShell.
4. Linux administration: RHEL, Ubuntu, systemd, LVM, Bash.
more: He also uses Python for automation, Docker, Splunk, SonarQube and Ansible. Ask about any area for detail, for example "Tell me about his Kubernetes experience."

topics.title: AWS and other clouds
topics.answer: His hands-on cloud work is on Microsoft Azure. His resume lists AWS at a fundamentals level only, and no Google Cloud. Roles that need deep AWS or GCP experience are not a direct match.

topics.title: Azure DevOps and CI/CD
topics.answer: CI/CD is the centre of his work. At Nexamatic he converted 60+ classic release pipelines into GitHub Actions workflows and reusable multi-stage Azure DevOps YAML templates. At Kumaran Systems he built pipelines for 35+ banking services with approval gates and change checks, and moved releases from bi-weekly to 3 per week with a change-failure rate under 5%.
more: His usual pipeline shape: pull-request validation, build and unit tests, security scans (SAST, dependency, container image, secret detection), versioned artifacts, then promotion Dev → UAT/Staging → Prod with approvals, using the same artifact at every stage. Rollback is a redeploy of the previous version, kept under 15 minutes.
Two demos show this: the Azure Pipelines Transaction API demo and the GitHub Actions DevSecOps demo. See the Projects page.

topics.title: GitHub Enterprise migration
topics.answer: At Nexamatic he led the migration of ~120 repositories and 45 teams from Azure Repos to GitHub Enterprise with under 30 minutes of total developer downtime. He standardised branch protection and CODEOWNERS, which brought pull-request review coverage to 100%.

topics.title: Site Reliability Engineering
topics.answer: He built an SRE practice at Nexamatic on SLIs, SLOs, error budgets and 40+ runbooks, and improved triage and escalation, which reduced MTTR by about 35%. He runs blameless post-incident reviews and the on-call rotation for a 10-member team, closing 90% of corrective actions within 30 days.
more: His alerting approach is to page on error-budget burn rate over two windows (for example 14.4x over 1 hour and 5 minutes) instead of on every error spike. That and alert-rule clean-up cut alert noise by 40%.

The SRE observability demo shows this end to end: Prometheus recording rules, multi-window burn-rate alerts with unit tests, Alertmanager routing, a Grafana dashboard, a runbook and an example RCA, all on synthetic data.

topics.title: Monitoring and observability
topics.answer: He works with Prometheus, Grafana, Azure Monitor, Log Analytics (KQL), Application Insights and Splunk. At Nexamatic he implemented dashboards with 150+ alert rules and routed logs to Splunk, cutting alert noise by 40%.
more: He prefers alerts tied to SLOs, every paging alert linked to a runbook, and tickets (not pages) for slow-burning problems.

topics.title: Kubernetes and AKS
topics.answer: At Nexamatic he operates 6 production AKS clusters with 180+ nodes and 300+ pods, using Helm, NGINX Ingress, the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler and Cluster Autoscaler. He delivers quarterly Kubernetes and node-pool upgrades with zero customer-facing outages. He also holds the KCNA certification.
more: At Kumaran Systems he containerised 15 services with Docker, pushed images to Azure Container Registry, and deployed them to AKS through Helm-based pipelines.

The AKS + Helm demo has a Helm chart with liveness and readiness probes, HPA and a PodDisruptionBudget, a staged pipeline with an approval before production, and SLO alert rules. It is validated with helm lint and a local smoke test; it has not been deployed to a real AKS cluster.

topics.title: Terraform and infrastructure as code
topics.answer: At Nexamatic he authored 25+ versioned Terraform modules and Bicep templates with remote state, policy checks and nightly drift detection, bringing all environments under infrastructure as code. At Kumaran Systems he introduced Terraform across 4 environments, cutting setup from ~3 days to 4 hours. Earlier, at UST Global, he used ARM templates.
more: The Terraform hub-and-spoke demo builds hub and spoke VNets, NSGs, peering, private DNS, tagging and backup. It passes terraform fmt and validate in CI; it is not applied to a real subscription.

topics.title: Azure cloud infrastructure
topics.answer: He designed and operates a multi-subscription Azure landing zone at Nexamatic (8 subscriptions, 600+ resources, 99.95% availability) with management groups, custom RBAC roles and tagging, reaching 98% tagging compliance and passing two client audits without major findings.
more: At UST Global he ran an Azure IaaS/PaaS estate of 250+ resources and cut monthly Azure spend by ~18% through right-sizing. At Nexamatic, automation with Azure Functions and Logic Apps saved ~20 engineer-hours a month and 22% of non-production compute cost.

topics.title: Azure networking
topics.answer: At UST Global he engineered hub-and-spoke virtual networks with subnets, NSGs, load balancers, private DNS and site-to-site VPN links to 2 on-premises data centres. At Cognizant he set up landing-zone foundations with 12 virtual networks and 2 site-to-site VPN tunnels.

topics.title: Security and DevSecOps
topics.answer: He raised Microsoft Defender for Cloud Secure Score from 62% to 85% at Nexamatic and embedded SAST, container image scanning, secret detection and Key Vault integration into pipelines, blocking 200+ vulnerable builds before production.
more: At Kumaran Systems he moved 300+ secrets into Azure Key Vault with managed identities and added SonarQube quality gates that caught 120+ critical vulnerabilities before release. At UST Global he removed 150+ excess role assignments in a least-privilege review.

topics.title: Cloud migration
topics.answer: He has rehosted 165 on-premises servers to Azure: 120 as Tech Lead at Cognizant (6 waves, 98% first-attempt cutover success) and 45 at UST Global (5 waves, zero data loss), using Azure Migrate and Azure Site Recovery.
more: At UST Global he also set up Azure Backup and Site Recovery for 60 critical workloads, meeting a 4-hour RTO and 15-minute RPO in semi-annual DR drills.
The migration-plan demo has a sample inventory, dependency map, a tested wave-planning script, and cutover and rollback runbooks, all on fictional servers.

topics.title: Windows Server administration
topics.answer: He spent five years administering Windows Server alongside Linux at Anewa Engineering: Active Directory with 1,200+ accounts, Group Policy, file shares and NTFS permissions, DNS and DHCP, and monthly patching with WSUS. He upgraded 30 servers from Windows Server 2008 R2 to 2016 with no data loss. At Cognizant he handled identity sync for 5,000+ AD accounts during a migration.
more: The server ops toolkit demo has PowerShell scripts for server health, patch status, AD account hygiene and a safe, allow-listed service restart, with Pester tests for the shared module.

topics.title: Linux administration
topics.answer: He administered RHEL and Ubuntu servers for five years at Anewa Engineering: installation, patching with yum and apt, troubleshooting CPU, memory and disk issues with top, vmstat, iostat and journalctl, and Bash automation that saved ~10 hours of manual work a week.
more: The server ops toolkit demo has Bash scripts for health checks, an SSH hardening check and a user audit, tested against fixture files. The patching lab demo covers pre- and post-patch checks.

topics.title: Certifications
topics.answer: He holds three certifications: Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104), Microsoft Certified: Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900), and Kubernetes and Cloud Native Associate (KCNA) from The Linux Foundation.

topics.title: Education
topics.answer: He has a Master of Computer Applications (MCA) from Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University, Hyderabad (2010) and a B.Sc. in Computer Science from Acharya Nagarjuna University (2007).

topics.title: Resume
topics.answer: The full resume is on the Resume page of this site as a view-only web page. For a copy, please contact Vamsikrishna directly on LinkedIn.

topics.title: Portfolio demos
topics.answer:
There are eight independent demos on the Projects page:
1. GitHub Actions DevSecOps pipeline
2. Azure Pipelines for a Transaction API
3. SRE observability and incident management
4. AKS + Helm delivery with SRE practices
5. Terraform hub-and-spoke network
6. Windows and Linux migration plan to Azure
7. Windows and Linux server ops toolkit
8. Patching and OS upgrade lab
more: All of them use fictional systems and synthetic data. They are not client work, and none is deployed to a real Azure subscription; each README says exactly what was tested and how.

topics.title: Demo: GitHub Actions DevSecOps pipeline
topics.answer: The DevSecOps demo is a GitHub Actions pipeline around a small inventory API. Five jobs run in parallel: Ruff lint, tests with an 80% coverage gate, Bandit SAST, Gitleaks secret scanning and pip-audit. Then a container job builds the image, smoke-tests it, checks it runs as a non-root user, scans it with Trivy and produces a CycloneDX SBOM.
more: Deployment is shown as a pattern only: a manual run on main reaches a demo-staging environment that prints what it would deploy. The docs explain the real path, using OIDC federated credentials to log in to Azure without stored secrets. The diagram is on the Projects page.

topics.title: Demo: Azure Pipelines for a Transaction API
topics.answer: This demo is a multi-stage Azure Pipelines YAML workflow for a sample Transaction API: pull-request checks and branch policy, Dev → UAT → Prod promotion of one package, an approval point before production, and written rollback steps. The Python API has unit tests.

topics.title: Demo: SRE observability and incident management
topics.answer: The SRE observability demo has an instrumented service, Prometheus recording rules and multi-window burn-rate alerts (with promtool unit tests), Alertmanager routing that separates pages from tickets, a Grafana dashboard, runbooks and a fictional RCA. An offline calculator works out error budget used and which alerts would fire.
more: On its synthetic data (3 days of traffic, then an ongoing incident), the calculator reports 99.763% availability, 47.4% of the error budget used, and a page-level alert at 34x burn over 1 hour. The numbers are synthetic, not from a real system.

topics.title: Demo: AKS + Helm delivery with SRE
topics.answer: The AKS + Helm demo packages a small API as a Helm chart with liveness and readiness probes, an HPA and a PodDisruptionBudget. The pipeline runs CI checks, deploys to staging, and waits for approval before production. It includes a 99.5% SLO with burn-rate alerts and an incident runbook.
more: It is validated with helm lint, helm template and a local smoke test of the app. It has not been deployed to a real AKS cluster.

topics.title: Demo: Terraform hub-and-spoke
topics.answer: The Terraform demo builds a hub VNet with shared services and two spoke VNets, NSGs that default to deny, peering, private DNS, standard tags and backup, with notes on DR design and cost. It passes terraform fmt and terraform validate in CI and is not applied to a real subscription.

topics.title: Demo: Windows and Linux migration plan
topics.answer: The migration-plan demo has a sample server inventory and dependency map, a Python script (with tests) that groups servers into migration waves based on dependencies, a cutover checklist and a rollback runbook. All servers are fictional.

topics.title: Demo: Windows and Linux server ops toolkit
topics.answer: The server ops toolkit has read-only PowerShell scripts for Windows Server health, patch status and Active Directory hygiene, and Bash scripts for Linux health checks, an SSH hardening check and a user audit. The one script that changes state, a service restart, only touches allow-listed services and asks before each restart.
more: The Bash scripts are tested against fixture files; the PowerShell module has Pester tests. Calls that need a real Windows Server or Active Directory were not run in CI.

topics.title: Demo: Patching and OS upgrade lab
topics.answer: The patching lab has PowerShell and Bash pre- and post-patch checks, a Linux patch script with a dry-run mode for dnf, yum and apt, and a tested script that builds a patch compliance report.

topics.title: About this assistant
topics.answer: I'm Vamsikrishna's Portfolio AI Assistant, not Vamsikrishna himself. I answer from a fixed set of notes taken from his resume and the demo documentation, entirely in your browser. I don't send your questions to a server, and nothing is stored after you leave the page.
more: Voice input uses your browser's built-in speech recognition. In some browsers, such as Chrome, the browser vendor processes that audio, so use text if you prefer.
